summary: Keepalive/heartbeat timing collision causes streaming connection half-close and mid-generation stall
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that streaming chat responses (SSE and WebSocket) occasionally transition to a half-closed state and stop producing tokens mid-generation. Unlike previous 'quiet period' stalls, these incidents correlate with periodic keepalive/heartbeat intervals from the customer's proxy and our load balancer.

Impact:
- Several long-running chat sessions for AcmeHealth (enterprise tenant) truncated without final token or final event; clients receive no explicit error.
- Occurs ~1-2x per 10k streaming sessions, higher on sessions >30s.
- Customer reports user-visible UX degradation in clinician-facing chat UI.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted (prod) routed through our edge LB -> nginx ingress pool -> serving runtime pool (dedicated cluster for AcmeHealth).
- Observed on us-east region only.
- Models: redwood/open-chat-v2 (default), fallback to redwood/gguf-compat-v1 occasionally.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start SSE stream with long prompt (expected >60 tokens).
2) Keep client idle (no new requests) while generation runs ~30-120s.
3) Observe stream stops emitting tokens; HTTP connection remains open (client sees no FIN) but no more data arrives.
4) After client attempts to reconnect, subsequent requests succeed.

Observed behavior:
- TCP-level traces show duplicate TCP keepalive probes around the time of silence for affected sessions.
- Proxy (customer-side) sends HTTP/1.1 keepalives; our LB also sends periodic pings. Timing collision window ~1s where both endpoints send probes.
- Nginx ingress logs show connection stayed ESTABLISHED; downstream worker logs show request marked as completed with no finalizing event.

Expected behavior:
- Streams continue until model generation completes or an explicit error is returned. Keepalive exchanges should not interrupt chunked transfer or server-sent events.

Immediate customer workaround suggested:
- Ask customer to increase client-side keepalive interval or disable aggressive proxy-level application-layer heartbeats while we investigate.

Attachments / traces:
- pcap snippets (s3://redwood-support/sup-873457/pcap-keepalive-collision.pcap)
- nginx-ingress logs excerpt (s3://redwood-support/sup-873457/nginx-logs.txt)
- runtime worker trace (trace-id: trace-20260312-8432)

investigation_notes:
Findings summary:
- Root hypothesis: race between application-layer keepalives (customer proxy + our LB) and serving runtime's token emission/flush path. When probe collision occurs during a memory compaction / worker preemption, the kernel-level socket state transitions to a half-closed state for the worker process, which then fails to append the final chunk/event.
- Reproducible in controlled environment when configuring both sides to 30s keepalive.
resolution:
Workaround: recommended customer increase their proxy keepalive to 120s; support applied temporary ingress config changes (disable proxy buffering on streaming routes, extend LB idle timeout to 180s) which reduced occurrences by ~80%.
Next steps / permanent fix: Engineering to harden runtime flush path to tolerate late keepalive probes (task INT-4123). Plan: ensure token flush uses sendmsg with MSG_MORE semantics and adds explicit final event ACK. Also add e2e test simulating keepalive collision window.
Follow-up: monitor SLO for next 7 days; schedule postmortem and update confluence runbook. Customer notified of temporary fix and roadmap for permanent resolution.
resolution_status: Mitigated - temporary ingress config + customer workaround; permanent fix scheduled
notes_for_followup:
